title: Code completion sorting ranks better matches lower
body: ### Tested versions 4.3, 4.4, has been present since 4.0 at least partially ### System information x ### Issue description There is something off and illogical with how code completions are sorted. I've personally noticed this mainly with completion for `print()`, just because it's used often and annoys me every time, but of course there are also in many other situations where it occurs. When writing `pri`, i would expect `print()` to be the first suggestion. it is the shortest and closest match to what i have written so far. but it is the fourth option in the list. this doesn't even change when i've written the full word and if i were to press tab now, i'd get a totally different function than the exact match i just typed. This is likely just from "alphabetical" sorting, where `_` just has a higher score than any other character. but it shouldn't - "no character" should always rank higher. like it does in other editors, like vscode ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4805046a-32a0-48d7-ba6b-35033129f4ef) further, since a few updates ago we can now type parts of words, or initials to get a better matching completion quicker. this is very nice. but it's still unpredictable. if i were to type `prr`, for **pr**int_**r**ich() i get the following matches with the second character in the second word for some reason? print_rich nowhere to be seen. let's add one more letter, `prri` again, why does the 2nd and 3rd character in the second word rank higher than the 1st and 2nd in the second word. even the 2nd and 3rd in the third word rank higher. There are a few open completion issues and proposals that would improve the completion experience overall, but don't mention this core issue. - https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/9178 - https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10665 - https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11079 Why this is a bug issue and not a proposal: The behaviour (especially the 2nd character situation) feels broken when using autocompletion and is unexpected both logically and compared to other code editors. Small note: this has been bugging me since 4.0, mostly for print(), but never enough to bring it up. i've recently talked with a few other users who had the same experience, finding it illogical and unexpected, that prompted me to open an issue ### Steps to reproduce typing any keyword with autocompletion that has other similar keywords ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) empty project
